title: Persevering Together Through Every Mile
summary: Training for a half marathon required early mornings, long runs, consistency, tenacity and something none of us expected: each other.
body_markdown:
**By Paige Hagan, Sales Operations Manager**


The finish line lasted only a moment. The real challenge happened in the months leading up to it.


Training for a half marathon required early mornings, long runs, consistency, and the tenacity to keep going when motivation faded. It also required something none of us expected: each other.


When Maria Salgueiro, Associate Director, FP&A, encouraged a few of us from our site at Bedford, Massachusetts, to register for the Cambridge Half Marathon, what seemed like a personal fitness goal quickly became a shared commitment.


Maria, Jack Feiler, Production Planner, Andre Crawford, Senior Mechanical Engineer, and I spent months preparing for 13.1 miles, supporting one another through every milestone and setback along the way.


Looking back, what stands out most isn’t race day itself. It’s the preparation: the long runs, weekend commitments, check-ins, and conversations that kept us moving forward when the goal still felt far away.


### **The Power of Support**


Maria was the catalyst for the entire experience. Having completed several half marathons before, she encouraged the rest of us to take on the challenge and helped keep us motivated throughout the process.


As the weeks passed, distances that once felt intimidating became routine. Goals that seemed out of reach slowly came within grasp, fueled by the encouragement and accountability we shared.


One of my favorite memories was completing a 12-mile training run with Jack. The miles passed quickly because we spent the entire run talking. It reinforced something we experienced throughout training: difficult challenges feel more manageable when you tackle them together. The same was true on race day when Maria and I spent all 13.1 miles running side by side.


### **Different Journeys, Shared Achievement**


Jack described the experience as a mental challenge as much as a physical one. Completing the race gave him confidence that extends beyond running, proving that persistence and preparation can help us accomplish more than we initially think possible.


Andre shared a similar perspective. While the training demanded commitment and consistency, crossing the finish line made every mile worthwhile.


For Maria, the most rewarding part was seeing teammates embrace a difficult goal and follow through. The experience created friendships outside of work and built a deeper appreciation for one another.


We also received support from Brendan Boyd, Beam Steering R&D Manager, whose running experience helped calm race-day nerves and provided encouragement throughout the process. He even came out to cheer us on during the race.


### **Going Farther Together**


By the time race day arrived, we had already accomplished something meaningful. The finish line was simply the celebration of months of commitment, accountability, and support.


While the race tested our endurance, the experience left us with something far more lasting: stronger relationships, greater confidence, and the knowledge that difficult goals become more attainable when[people work toward them together](https://novanta.com/careers-culture/life-at-novanta/) as One Novanta.
